# Changes to miniaudio.h

`miniaudio.h` is miniaudio 0.11.25 (public domain or MIT No Attribution, see `LICENSE`),
https://github.com/mackron/miniaudio. It is unchanged except for the functions
below. Re-apply it when updating, or drop it if upstream has an equivalent.

| Where | What and why |
|---|---|
| `ma_dr_flac__seek_to_pcm_frame__binary_search_internal` (dr_flac, marked "FatzAudio patch") | Seeking a `.flac` without a SEEKTABLE (FFmpeg's encoder writes none, nor did FatzAudio's before it wrote one to seekable outputs) used a bisection that took up to 11 probes (one frame decode each) per seek on a 14 s test file, and up to 16 on real music. The replacement interpolates between the closest known frames either side, aiming one block before the target, and bisects twice whenever a probe fails to halve the range, so typical files seek in 2 to 4 probes. The same function searches between the points of a SEEKTABLE, which gets faster too (8 probes down to 5 with a point every 3.7 s). Probes read only the frame header (`ma_dr_flac__seek_to_approximate_flac_frame_to_byte` calls the new `ma_dr_flac__fa_read_next_stream_frame_header`, which also skips headers whose block size, channels or sample rate don't fit the stream, and the search skips one whose frame number is out of order with the frames it has found, or past the end); the frame the search ends on is decoded and CRC-16 checked (or the next good one, when it fails), so a seek lands on exactly the same samples. On a 24-bit file that cut the reads per seek by a third. Long digital silence before music is the worst case: up to 15 probes against upstream's 11. A probe that finds a new upper frame within two blocks past the target does not count as failing to halve the range, so it doesn't bisect (finding the same upper frame again still does). `ma_dr_flac__read_next_flac_frame_header` treats a header with the wrong bits per sample, or a 16-bit block size of 65536, as a false sync and looks on (upstream ends the search there, before the CRC-8 is even read, and a seek in 24-bit audio then decoded from the start: 15 ms instead of 0.5). Tested by `test_flac_seek_search` in `tests/test_core.c`. |
| `wasapi.rawCapture` in `ma_device_config` (plumbed through `ma_device_init__wasapi`, `ma_device_reinit__wasapi` and `ma_device_init_internal__wasapi`, marked "FatzAudio patch") | Mixer mics ask Windows for the RAW capture stream (`AUDCLNT_STREAMOPTIONS_RAW` through `IAudioClient2::SetClientProperties`, before `Initialize`), which skips the system's capture effects: automatic gain, noise suppression and echo cancelling, made for calls, which spoil singing and add latency. Upstream 0.11.25 never sets the stream options. A driver without RAW support refuses the property and the stream opens as before, so the patch never makes an open fail. Off unless asked for; `FA_MIC_OS_PROCESSING` keeps it off. |
| `ma_dr_flac__decode_flac_frame` (wrapper), `ma_dr_flac__read_and_decode_next_flac_frame`, `ma_dr_flac__fa_frame_has_samples`, `ma_dr_flac__fa_drop_stale_frame` and the seek fast paths of `ma_dr_flac_seek_to_pcm_frame` (marked "FatzAudio patch") | A damaged `.flac` crashed the decoder with a null read: a frame that failed to decode (or whose header was read by a seek and never decoded) left its block size and some channels' sample pointers in `currentFLACFrame`, and the next seek backwards "inside the current frame", or the next read, trusted them. A failed decode now clears the subframes and the frame's remaining count, the reads drop a current frame that has no samples or whose remaining count exceeds its block, and the two in-frame seek shortcuts need a frame with samples. Found by the fuzz targets (`tests/fuzz`); inputs in `tests/fuzz/regress/stream`. Every seek that reads a frame header without decoding the frame (the frame-by-frame and seek-table searches, the Ogg search, the probes of the interpolation search) goes through `ma_dr_flac__fa_read_frame_header_only`, which first drops the decoded frame's samples and remaining count: a search that then failed (no next header, as in a cut-off file) left the old samples behind a header of another frame, and the next seek back inside "the current frame" read them at the wrong offset. Tested by `tests/test_drflac.c`. |
